alg-threshold-partial-pivot-sparse-lu.actual_claim_text:
Input a nonsingular real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ with $n\ge1$, an initial simultaneous row-and-column permutation matrix $P$ under the row-action convention of [[def-permutation-matrix-partial-pivoting-and-pivot-growth]], and a threshold $\theta\in(0,1]$. Initialize the active matrix $S^{(0)}=PAP^T$, the accumulated row permutation $Q=I_n$, the unit lower-triangular factor $L=I_n$, and the upper-triangular factor $U=0$. Treat an unstored active entry as zero. Every real scalar operation uses [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]; if an exact intermediate is nonzero and subnormal, overflows, or the operation reports range failure, return **range-failure** with its stage. Pivot tests and tie-breaking comparisons are exact guards on current stored values. For $k=0,\ldots,n-1$, ties for a maximum are resolved by choosing the smallest current row index.

At stage $k$, let $m_k=\max_{i\ge k}|S^{(k)}_{ik}|$. If $m_k=0$, return **singular-pivot**$(k)$. If $|S^{(k)}_{kk}|\ge\theta m_k$, select row $p=k$; otherwise select the smallest row attaining $m_k$. If $p\ne k$, swap rows $p$ and $k$ of the active matrix and the already stored entries in columns $0,\ldots,k-1$ of those rows of $L$. Also replace $Q$ by $E_{kp}Q$, where $E_{kp}$ is the permutation matrix swapping rows $k$ and $p$. Do not change the previously stored rows of $U$. If the selected pivot is zero, return **singular-pivot**$(k)$.

Save the active pivot row by setting $U_{kj}=S^{(k)}_{kj}$ for every $j\ge k$; entries $U_{kj}$ with $j<k$ remain zero. Set $L_{ik}=S^{(k)}_{ik}/S^{(k)}_{kk}$ for every $i>k$, interpreting a missing $S^{(k)}_{ik}$ as zero. For every $i,j>k$, update
$$S^{(k+1)}_{ij}=S^{(k)}_{ij}-L_{ik}U_{kj}.$$
In a sparse representation it suffices to visit positions where $S^{(k)}_{ij}\ne0$ or $L_{ik}U_{kj}\ne0$; missing entries in this formula are zero. Allocate any position whose rounded update is nonzero; this is numerical fill. If an arithmetic operation is not representable or reports a range error, return **range-failure** with its stage. Any failure return is a status only and asserts no factorization. On success return $(Q,P,L,U)$. In exact arithmetic the updates give $QPAP^T=LU$; the procedure makes no claim of a universal fill or growth bound.

source_notes.subject: Threshold sparse LU with deterministic row pivoting
source_notes.domain: a nonsingular real matrix of positive dimension and positive threshold at most one
source_notes.result: stored factors with accumulated row permutation or singular-pivot/range status
source_notes.choice: When a threshold fails the smallest row attaining the current column maximum is selected; earlier multiplier rows are swapped explicitly.

cases.empty: N:The Definition assumes n at least one and a nonsingular input, so no empty factorization input is declared.
cases.one: C:One nonzero scalar has only its pivot row, no multiplier rows and no trailing updates.
cases.zero: C:A zero active column maximum returns singular-pivot immediately; individual unstored entries are treated as zero.
cases.degenerate: C:The zero-pivot and zero-column-maximum tests are explicit failure guards; arithmetic underflow/overflow returns range-failure.
cases.endpoints: C:Theta one is allowed and requires a maximal pivot; theta zero is excluded before any theta-inverse multiplier estimate.

def-elimination-tree-and-column-reach.actual_claim_text:
Let $A=A^*$ and use the Hermitian structural graph of [[def-hermitian-structural-graph-adapter]]. The graph definition [[def-symmetric-structural-elimination-graph-and-ordering]] supplies the ordering $v_0,\ldots,v_{n-1}$, filled graphs, parent map, and elimination forest. For each $k$, let $N_k(v_k)$ be the later-neighbor set at elimination of $v_k$, and define its structural column set
$$\mathcal C_k=\{v_k\}\cup N_k(v_k).$$
Its off-diagonal size is the column count $\ell_k=|N_k(v_k)|$. An **ancestor** of $v_k$ is obtained by following one or more supplied parent edges; a **descendant** is the inverse relation. The **reach** of $v_k$ is the set of vertices visited by following its parent path, including $v_k$.

source_notes.subject: Structural column sets and parent-path reach
source_notes.domain: a supplied Hermitian graph and elimination ordering
source_notes.result: column set is pivot union later neighbors and reach follows the parent path
source_notes.choice: The parent map comes from the fixed elimination forest and path following is functional, not a choice of an ancestor.

cases.empty: C:With no later neighbors the column still contains its pivot, its off-diagonal count is zero and the parent path ends at that root.
cases.one: C:For a one-vertex forest the column/reach contain only that vertex and there is no strict ancestor.
cases.zero: C:A diagonal Hermitian matrix has no off-diagonal edges, so every off-diagonal column count is zero and each reach stops at its vertex.
cases.degenerate: N:Only the graph/ordering is used; numerical pivot singularity is not an assumption of these structural definitions.
cases.endpoints: N:No interval or real-valued endpoint parameter appears in the parent-path definitions.

def-hermitian-structural-graph-adapter.actual_claim_text:
Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ satisfy $A=A^*$, where $A^*=\overline A^{\,T}$. Define a real symmetric pattern matrix $H\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$ by $H_{ii}=0$ and, for $i<j$, set $H_{ij}=H_{ji}=1$ exactly when $A_{ij}\ne0$; otherwise set both entries to zero. Since $A_{ji}=\overline{A_{ij}}$, this pattern records exactly the undirected off-diagonal support of $A$.

Apply the graph and elimination-ordering convention of [[def-symmetric-structural-elimination-graph-and-ordering]] to $H$. Its structural graph is the **Hermitian structural graph** of $A$, and its filled graphs are the symbolic pattern used for Hermitian elimination. The real matrix $H$ records only support; numerical Schur complements are formed from $A$.

source_notes.subject: The Hermitian off-diagonal support adapter
source_notes.domain: a Hermitian complex matrix with fixed row/column indices
source_notes.result: a zero-diagonal symmetric real pattern records exactly its off-diagonal support
source_notes.choice: For each pair of indices the pattern is fixed by the nonzero-entry test and Hermitian conjugate symmetry.

cases.empty: C:For a dimension-zero carrier no index pair is tested and the support pattern is empty; this adapter performs no pivot or division.
cases.one: C:For a one-by-one Hermitian matrix the diagonal pattern entry is zero and there is no off-diagonal graph edge.
cases.zero: C:A zero Hermitian matrix maps to the all-zero pattern; the adapter records support rather than asserting invertibility.
cases.degenerate: N:Hermitian symmetry is the only matrix condition; singular and rank-deficient matrices still have the same well-defined support test.
cases.endpoints: N:This support conversion has finite indices but no real interval or threshold parameter.

ex-nonsingular-indefinite-requires-two-b.actual_claim_text:
Take
$$A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
This Hermitian matrix is nonsingular and indefinite. Every one-by-one diagonal pivot test fails, while the declared two-by-two pivot passes and gives an exact block $LDL^*$ factorization.

current_proof_steps.text: The determinant of $A$ is $-1$, so $A$ is nonsingular. Its eigenvectors $(1,1)^T$ and $(1,-1)^T$ have eigenvalues $1$ and $-1$, respectively; therefore $A$ is indefinite. [given, algebra]
Both diagonal candidates have pivot $0$, while the other entry in each column has modulus $1$. Since $\theta^{-1}|0|=0$, neither one-by-one test in [F1] passes. [given, F1, algebra]

For the declared block $D=A$, $\det D=-1\ne0$ and $D^{-1}=A$. There are no external indices, so $c_1=c_2=0$ and the two-by-two threshold left side is zero; the test in [F1] passes. [given, F1, algebra]

The algorithm therefore returns $P=I$, $L=I$, and $D_{\rm blk}=A$. Direct multiplication gives $A=LD_{\rm blk}L^*$. Thus the block pivot succeeds where every one-by-one diagonal pivot fails. [step 1.3, algebra] ∎

source_notes.subject: The zero-diagonal exchange-matrix pivot example
source_notes.domain: the fixed two-by-two Hermitian matrix with unit off-diagonals
source_notes.result: scalar diagonal pivots fail but the full two-by-two block is nonsingular
source_notes.choice: The proposed block is the whole given matrix, so no search for an unspecified pivot is used.

cases.empty: N:The example is a fixed matrix of order two, not an empty elimination sequence.
cases.one: C:The one-by-one pivot alternative fails because both diagonal entries are exactly zero; the successful alternative uses the declared two-by-two block.
cases.zero: C:Both diagonal zeros are part of the example; they demonstrate scalar failure without making the full matrix singular.
cases.degenerate: C:The verification computes determinant minus one, so zero diagonal entries do not imply a degenerate two-by-two block.
cases.endpoints: N:No continuous parameter or limiting endpoint is varied in this exchange-matrix calculation.

ex-star-orderings-produce-different-spar.actual_claim_text: For an integer $m\ge3$, let $G$ be the star with center $0$ and leaves $1,\ldots,m$. Let $A=I+t\,\operatorname{Adj}(G)$, where $t=1/(2\sqrt m)$ and $\operatorname{Adj}(G)$ is the adjacency matrix. In leaf-first order, elimination adds no fill. In center-first order, symbolic elimination adds every edge between leaves, and the actual Cholesky Schur complement has all those entries nonzero.

current_proof_steps.text:
Write a vector as $x=(x_0,y_1,\ldots,y_m)$. The quadratic form is $x^TAx=x_0^2+\sum_i y_i^2+2t x_0\sum_i y_i$. Since $m\sum_i y_i^2-(\sum_i y_i)^2=\sum_{i<j}(y_i-y_j)^2\ge0$, we have $|\sum_i y_i|\le\sqrt m\,\|y\|_2$. Therefore [given, algebra]
$$2t|x_0|\left|\sum_i y_i\right|\le 2t\sqrt m\,|x_0|\|y\|_2\le t\sqrt m(x_0^2+\|y\|_2^2)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2.$$
It follows that $x^TAx\ge\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2>0$ for $x\ne0$, so $A$ is positive definite. [given, algebra]

In leaf-first order, each leaf has exactly one later neighbor, the center. By [F1] no pair of distinct remaining neighbors exists, so eliminating that leaf adds no edge. This holds for every leaf; eliminating the last center also adds no edge. [given, F1, algebra]

In center-first order, the center's later-neighbor set is all $m$ leaves. By [F1], the graph update inserts every pair of distinct leaves, so it has $\binom m2$ leaf-to-leaf fill edges not in the original star. [given, F1, algebra]

The pivot at the center is $1$. Its Schur complement on the leaves is $I_m-t^2\mathbf1\mathbf1^T$, whose off-diagonal entries are $-t^2\ne0$. Thus the symbolic fill edges from step 1.3 are also numerical nonzeros for this matrix, while step 1.2 gives no fill in the other order. [step 1.2, step 1.3, given, algebra]
Steps 1.2 and 2.1 exhibit respectively $0$ and $\binom m2$ fill edges for two orderings of the same positive-definite sparse matrix. [step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

source_notes.subject: Leaf-first versus center-first elimination of a star
source_notes.domain: at least three leaves and explicit positive edge weight one over twice the square root of their count
source_notes.result: no leaf-first fill versus a full nonzero leaf clique after center elimination
source_notes.choice: The two orderings and edge weight are explicitly fixed; no separator minimizer or generic no-cancellation choice is needed.

cases.empty: N:The star has a center and at least three leaves, excluding an empty graph.
cases.one: N:The leaf count is at least three; a singleton star is not used for the asserted fill contrast.
cases.zero: C:The initially missing leaf-to-leaf entries are zero; the center Schur update makes them all minus t squared, which is nonzero.
cases.degenerate: N:The chosen edge weight is strictly positive and the example proves positive definiteness; arbitrary singular star matrices are not covered.
cases.endpoints: N:There is no interval-valued parameter here; the leaf count is an integer at least three and the weight is prescribed.

ex-two-dimensional-poisson-nested-dissec.actual_claim_text: For $k\ge1$, let $G_k$ be the grid on coordinate vertices $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}^2$, relabeled by the lexicographic zero-based bijection in [[alg-nested-dissection-ordering-on-regular-grids]], and let $A_k=4I-\operatorname{Adj}(G_k)$, the Dirichlet five-point Poisson matrix. The coordinate nested-dissection ordering recursively places its median row and column after the child rectangles. This example checks positive definiteness and instantiates the two-dimensional factorization bounds.

current_proof_steps.text:
For every grid vertex $v$, let $b(v)=4-\deg_{G_k}(v)$ be its number of missing boundary neighbors. Expanding squares gives [given, algebra]
$$x^TA_kx=\sum_{\{v,w\}\in E(G_k)}(x_v-x_w)^2+\sum_{v\in G_k}b(v)x_v^2.$$
The right side is nonnegative. If it is zero, every adjacent pair has equal coordinates and every boundary vertex with $b(v)>0$ has value zero. The grid is connected and has a boundary vertex, so all coordinates are equal to zero. Hence $A_k$ is positive definite. [given, algebra]

By [F1], the order is the coordinate nested-dissection order on the five-point grid. The matrix is symmetric positive definite by step 1.1 and its off-diagonal pattern is exactly $G_k$. For $k\ge2$, applying [F2] with $n=k^2$ gives work $O((k^2)^{3/2})=O(k^3)$ and factor storage $O(k^2\log(k^2))=O(k^2\log k)$. For $k=1$, the matrix and factor each have one entry. [step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]
Step 1.1 verifies the matrix hypothesis and step 2.1 gives the nested-dissection cost specialization. [step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

source_notes.subject: Five-point Poisson matrix on a square grid
source_notes.domain: positive side length with matrix four I minus grid adjacency
source_notes.result: positive definiteness and the two-dimensional nested-dissection cost instance
source_notes.choice: The grid labels and median-recursion ordering are supplied; the example does not choose an optimal ordering.

cases.empty: N:The coordinate side length is at least one, so there is always a vertex and the matrix is nonempty.
cases.one: C:At side length one the adjacency is zero and the matrix is the scalar four, with one positive pivot and constant work/storage.
cases.zero: C:Missing grid edges have zero coefficients; these zeros leave the five-point graph a subgraph of the permitted grid rather than violating the positive diagonal.
cases.degenerate: N:The example establishes positive definiteness of the prescribed Dirichlet matrix and does not assert a singular Neumann analogue.
cases.endpoints: N:Grid boundary coordinates are discrete vertices; no continuous parameter endpoint is part of the asymptotic cost claim.

lem-elimination-tree-reach-contains-each.actual_claim_text:
Let $v_k$ be a vertex in the elimination forest supplied by [[def-elimination-tree-and-column-reach]]. Every later filled neighbor of $v_k$ lies on its parent path and is therefore an ancestor. Consequently, if $v_s$ is a child of $v_k$, then every later neighbor of $v_s$ other than $v_k$ is a later neighbor of $v_k$; equivalently,
$$\mathcal C_s\setminus\{v_s\}\subseteq\mathcal C_k.$$

current_proof_steps.text: Fix $v_k$ and a later filled neighbor $v_t$. If $v_t$ is the parent, it is an ancestor by definition. Otherwise let $v_s$ be the parent. By [F2], $k<s<t$. Since $v_s$ and $v_t$ are both later neighbors of $v_k$, [F3] inserts $\{v_s,v_t\}$ when $v_k$ is eliminated. Thus $v_t$ remains a later neighbor of $v_s$. [given, F2, F3, choose]

Now let $v_s$ be a child of $v_k$. Every later neighbor $v_t$ of $v_s$ is either $v_k$ or is later than $v_k$. In the latter case both $v_k$ and $v_t$ are later neighbors of $v_s$, so [F3] joins them in the filled graph. Thus every element of $\mathcal C_s\setminus\{v_s\}$ belongs to $\mathcal C_k$. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

If $v_t$ is not the parent of $v_s$, replace $v_k$ by $v_s$ and repeat. At each repetition the ordering position strictly increases and is at most $t$, because the current vertex remains adjacent to $v_t$ and its parent is the earliest later neighbor. The finite increasing sequence must reach position $t$; it cannot stop earlier at a root while still having later neighbor $v_t$. Hence $v_t$ lies on the parent path from $v_k$ and is an ancestor. [step 1.1, F2, induction, algebra]
Step 2.1 proves the ancestor assertion, and step 1.2 gives the child-column containment used to assemble fronts. [step 2.1, step 1.2] ∎

source_notes.subject: Filled neighbors lie on the elimination parent path
source_notes.domain: a supplied pivot vertex and its elimination forest
source_notes.result: later neighbors are ancestors and a child contribution embeds in its parent front
source_notes.choice: The parent is already fixed by the forest; its successive vertices are followed uniquely.

cases.empty: C:If a pivot has no later neighbor, its ancestor-containment assertion is vacuous and there is no child contribution to embed.
cases.one: C:A lone root has no later neighbor and its structural column is the singleton pivot; containment does not require a nonexistent parent.
cases.zero: C:An edgeless later-neighbor set adds no off-diagonal reach; the proof can stop immediately at a root.
cases.degenerate: N:The statement concerns symbolic fill and parent paths, with no numerical pivot-value or rank condition.
cases.endpoints: N:The containment has no real interval parameter; it quantifies over the supplied finite vertex ordering.

lem-filled-edge-path-characterisation.actual_claim_text: Use the zero-based graph and ordering of [[def-symmetric-structural-elimination-graph-and-ordering]]. For distinct remaining vertices $x,y\in V_k$, the pair $\{x,y\}$ is an edge of $G_k$ if and only if the original graph $G_0$ contains a finite walk from $x$ to $y$ all of whose internal vertices belong to $\{v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}\}$. A walk may repeat vertices; its internal vertices are the entries other than its two endpoints.

current_proof_steps.text: At $k=0$, a walk with no internal vertices consists of one edge, so the claimed equivalence is exactly the definition of $G_0$. [given, F1, base, algebra]

Suppose the equivalence holds at stage $k$. A retained edge in $G_{k+1}$ already has a witnessing walk whose internal vertices are among $v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}$. An edge newly added at step $k$ joins two vertices $x,y$ that are each adjacent to $v_k$ in $G_k$. The induction hypothesis gives walks from $x$ to $v_k$ and from $v_k$ to $y$ with internal vertices among $v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}$; concatenating them gives the required walk with the additional internal vertex $v_k$. This proves the forward implication at stage $k+1$. [F1, IH, induction, algebra]

Conversely, let a witnessing walk from $x$ to $y$ have internal vertices among $v_0,\ldots,v_k$. If it has no internal occurrence of $v_k$, the induction hypothesis gives an edge in $G_k$, which is retained. Otherwise take the first and last internal occurrences of $v_k$. The initial subwalk from $x$ to the first occurrence and the terminal subwalk from the last occurrence to $y$ have all internal vertices among $v_0,\ldots,v_{k-1}$. By induction, $x$ and $y$ are both later neighbors of $v_k$ in $G_k$. Since $x\ne y$, the update inserts $\{x,y\}$ in $G_{k+1}$. [F1, IH, step 1.2, induction, algebra]
The base case and steps 1.2 and 2.1 prove both implications for every stage by induction on $k$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, discharge-induction] ∎

source_notes.subject: Characterisation of symbolic fill by earlier-vertex walks
source_notes.domain: two distinct remaining vertices after a fixed number of eliminations
source_notes.result: filled-edge membership is equivalent to an original walk with earlier internal vertices
source_notes.choice: The proof replaces finite walk segments and deletes finite repetitions; it does not select a path in an arbitrary infinite family.

cases.empty: N:A claimed pair consists of two distinct remaining vertices, so the premise supplies nonempty endpoint data.
cases.one: N:A one-vertex remaining graph contains no distinct endpoint pair to which this equivalence could be applied.
cases.zero: C:At zero eliminated vertices a qualifying walk has no earlier internal vertex, so for distinct endpoints it reduces to an original edge.
cases.degenerate: N:Walks may repeat vertices by definition; the argument does not require a simple or nondegenerate numerical matrix.
cases.endpoints: C:The two endpoints must remain outside the earlier eliminated set; only internal walk entries may belong to it.

lem-hermitian-schur-support-is-contained.actual_claim_text:
Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ be Hermitian and use the Hermitian structural graph adapter of [[def-hermitian-structural-graph-adapter]]. Fix an ordering and suppose each scalar pivot $p_k=S^k_{v_kv_k}$ is nonzero. Form the Hermitian Schur updates
$$S^{k+1}_{ij}=S^k_{ij}-S^k_{iv_k}p_k^{-1}S^k_{v_kj}.$$
Then every $S^k$ is Hermitian, every nonzero off-diagonal entry of $S^k$ is an edge of the corresponding filled graph, and the later neighbors of every eliminated vertex form a clique in the next filled graph.

current_proof_steps.text:
At stage $0$, $S^0=A$ is Hermitian. If $S^k$ is Hermitian, then its diagonal pivot $p_k$ is real. Since it is nonzero, substituting $a=p_k,b=0$ in [F4] gives $p_k^{-1}=p_k/p_k^2=1/p_k\in\mathbb R$; the denominator is nonzero by [F3]. For remaining $i,j$, [given, F1, F3, F4, base, IH, algebra]
$$\overline{S^{k+1}_{ji}}=\overline{S^k_{ji}-S^k_{jv_k}p_k^{-1}S^k_{v_ki}} =S^k_{ij}-S^k_{iv_k}p_k^{-1}S^k_{v_kj}=S^{k+1}_{ij}.$$
Thus the update preserves Hermitian symmetry. [given, F1, F3, F4, base, IH, algebra]
By [F2], the graph update itself joins every pair of distinct later neighbors of $v_k$. Thus each such later-neighbor set is a clique in the next filled graph. [given, F2, algebra]

The base case and step 2.1 prove the support inclusion at every stage; step 1.2 proves the clique property. The proof uses conjugate symmetry for Hermitian matrices and therefore supplies the complex-Hermitian extension beyond the real-symmetric supplier theorem. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, discharge-induction] ∎

source_notes.subject: Hermitian Schur support stays within symbolic fill
source_notes.domain: a fixed ordering with each used scalar pivot nonzero
source_notes.result: Hermitian symmetry persists and every new nonzero off-diagonal lies in the neighbor clique
source_notes.choice: Updates and cliques are determined by the given ordering and entries; no numerical noncancellation pattern is selected.

cases.empty: C:If a stage has no later neighbors its trailing clique is empty and the update creates no off-diagonal support.
cases.one: C:A scalar pivot with no remaining vertex needs no off-diagonal Schur update; Hermitian diagonal reality is retained.
cases.zero: C:A new off-diagonal can be nonzero only through an old entry or two nonzero pivot couplings; zero couplings cannot create a forbidden edge.
cases.degenerate: N:Zero scalar pivots are excluded by the explicit nonzero-pivot hypothesis, so this support lemma is not an existence theorem for admissible pivots.
cases.endpoints: N:There is no tolerance or real interval parameter in the exact Schur support statement.

lem-nested-dissection-fronts-are-boundar.actual_claim_text:
Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and use the coordinate grid and recursive ordering of [[alg-nested-dissection-ordering-on-regular-grids]]. For a recursion box $B$, let $S_B$ be its median separator; for the terminal one-vertex box take $S_B=B$. Let $\partial^+B$ be the set of grid vertices outside $B$ adjacent to some vertex of $B$. If $v\in S_B$, then every later filled neighbor of $v$ lies in $S_B\cup\partial^+B$. If every side of $B$ has length at most $s$, then
$$
|\{v\}\cup N^+_\pi(v)|\le |S_B|+|\partial^+B|\le 3d\,s^{d-1}.
$$

current_proof_steps.text: The root box has empty exterior boundary. If $B$ is a child of a box $C$, every grid neighbor just outside $B$ is either in $S_C$ or just outside $C$: distinct child boxes are separated by the removed coordinate hyperplanes. Thus $\partial^+B\subseteq S_C\cup\partial^+C$. Induction up the finite recursion tree, using that each ancestor separator is ordered after all vertices in its child boxes by [F1], shows that every vertex of $\partial^+B$ is ordered after every vertex of $B$. [F1, induction, algebra]

Fix $v\in S_B$ and a later filled neighbor $w$. If $w\in B$, then $w$ cannot lie in a child box because every child is ordered before $S_B$; hence $w\in S_B$. If $w\notin B$, [F2] gives an original grid walk from $v$ to $w$ whose internal vertices were eliminated before $v$. The first vertex of this walk outside $B$ lies in $\partial^+B$ and, by step 1.1, is ordered after $v$. It therefore cannot be an internal vertex of the walk, so it must be its endpoint $w$. Hence $w\in\partial^+B$. [given, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

If the side lengths of $B$ are $m_1,\ldots,m_d\le s$, each of its at most $d$ coordinate hyperplanes contains at most $s^{d-1}$ vertices, so $|S_B|\le d s^{d-1}$. The exterior grid neighbors lie across the $2d$ faces, each with at most $s^{d-1}$ vertices, so $|\partial^+B|\le2d s^{d-1}$. The containment in step 2.1 therefore gives the stated column-size bound. [step 2.1, F1, algebra]
Steps 2.1 and 3.1 establish both the filled-neighbor containment and its numerical bound for every separator vertex, including the terminal one-vertex case. [step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

source_notes.subject: Median-separator fronts are confined to local boundaries
source_notes.domain: dimension two or three and a recursion box whose maximum side length is s
source_notes.result: later neighbors lie in separator union outer boundary and front size is at most three d times s to the d-minus-one
source_notes.choice: Median hyperplanes and parent boxes are fixed geometrically; the proof bounds their cardinalities without choosing a separator.

cases.empty: N:The argument starts with a vertex in a separator of a nonempty recursion box; an empty box supplies no such vertex.
cases.one: C:The Statement explicitly sets a terminal one-vertex separator equal to its box; the front contains that vertex and satisfies the stated cardinal bound.
cases.zero: N:The recursion side length is positive for a box containing a vertex; a zero-side box has no front to bound.
cases.degenerate: N:The bound is structural for coordinate grids and is independent of numerical matrix rank or cancellations.
cases.endpoints: C:The outer boundary consists of vertices adjacent to a box, including boxes touching the global grid boundary where there are fewer outside neighbors.

lem-hermitian-block-ldl-kernel-roundoff-.actual_claim_text:
For a successful [[alg-certified-hermitian-one-and-two-by-two-ldl-kernel]], let $k\in\{1,2\}$ and $t$ be its trailing dimension. Every accepted $D$ is nonsingular and satisfies the original exact componentwise threshold test. For either size put $g_j=(1+6u)/(1-(j-1)u)-1$ for $j=1,2$. For $k=1$ put $\omega_1=u$. For $k=2$ put
$$\mu=\frac{\epsilon_d}{|\widehat d|}<1,\quad \nu=\sqrt2u(1+\mu)+\mu,$$
$$\chi=u+(1+u)(\sqrt2g_2(1+u)+u),\qquad \omega_2=\nu+\chi(1+\nu).$$
For either size define
$$q_k=(1+u)(1+g_k)(1+\omega_k)-1,\quad e_M=\omega_k\|B\|_F\|D^{-1}\|_2,$$
$$\beta=\sqrt2\bigl(u\|C\|_F+q_k\|B\|_F^2\|D^{-1}\|_2\bigr),\qquad \eta_{k,t}=\sqrt2\max\{u\sqrt t,kq_k\}.$$
Then, writing $M=BD^{-1}$ and $\Delta=\widehat S-(C-BD^{-1}B^*)$,
$$\|\widehat M-M\|_F\le e_M,\qquad \|\Delta\|_2\le\beta\le\eta_{k,t}(\|C\|_2+\|B\|_2^2\|D^{-1}\|_2).$$
For $t=0$ all residuals are zero and use $e_M=\beta=\eta_{k,0}=0$. The coefficients are explicit unit-roundoff bounds, $O(u)$ at fixed nonzero normalized determinant as $u\to0$; near-singular scaled pivots have no uniform smallness guarantee.

The actual stored multipliers also have coupling residual $N=\widehat MD-B$. Set $\widehat T=\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\\widehat M&I\end{pmatrix}$. The full reconstruction residual satisfies
$$F=\begin{pmatrix}D&B^*\\B&C\end{pmatrix}-\widehat T\operatorname{diag}(D,\widehat S)\widehat T^*=\begin{pmatrix}0&-N^*\\-N&-\Delta-(\widehat M-M)B^*-\widehat MN^*\end{pmatrix},$$
$$\|F\|_2\le f:=\beta+e_M\|B\|_2+(1+\|\widehat M\|_2)e_M\|D\|_2.$$
This additional residual is necessary for actual rounded output factors; the trailing-only residual applies to conceptual exact multipliers.

current_proof_steps.text: For two-by-two $D$, put $E=D/s$ and $J=\operatorname{adj}(E)$. Each real component of $E$ has magnitude at most one. Expansion of the determinant computation multiplies each of its three quadratic terms by at most five factors $1+\delta_i$, $|\delta_i|\le u$, including scaling. For $0<u<1$, the coefficient deviation is at most $(1+u)^5-1$, since the lower deviation $1-(1-u)^5$ is no greater. Also $|E_{11}E_{22}|+(\operatorname{Re}E_{12})^2+(\operatorname{Im}E_{12})^2\le3$. Thus $|\widehat d-\det E|\le\epsilon_d$. Acceptance gives $\det E\ne0$. The entrywise scaling bound $|J-\widehat J|\le u|J|$ implies $|J|\le|\widehat J|/(1-u)$ and $|J|\ge|\widehat J|/(1+u)$. The algorithm's $U,V$ therefore bound $|D^{-1}|$ above and below. The modulus guard follows by expanding its scaled sum, square root and rescaling, giving relative factors between $(1-u)^4$ and $(1+u)^4$. The resulting maximum/product interval tests prove exact acceptance or definite threshold failure; unresolved cases are explicitly inconclusive. Scalar pivots satisfy the same scalar threshold argument. [given, F1, algebra]

Define $R=\widehat J/(s\widehat d)$ for analysis only. Scaling gives $\|\widehat J-J\|_F\le u\|J\|_F\le\sqrt2u\|J\|_2$. The inverse formula gives $\|D^{-1}\|_2=\|J\|_2/(s|\det E|)$, and step 1.1 gives $|\det E|/|\widehat d|\le1+\mu$. Subtract the two inverse expressions to obtain $\|R-D^{-1}\|_2\le\nu\|D^{-1}\|_2$ and $\|R\|_2\le(1+\nu)\|D^{-1}\|_2$. This retains the actual scaled-determinant sensitivity. [F3, step 1.1, algebra]

The computed $B/s$ has Frobenius error at most $u\|B\|_F/s$. By [F2], its product with $\widehat J$ adds at most $g_2(1+u)\|B\|_F\|\widehat J\|_F/s$. Since $\|\widehat J\|_F\le\sqrt2\|\widehat J\|_2$, the product discrepancy relative to $B\widehat J/s$ is at most $(\sqrt2g_2(1+u)+u)\|B\|_F\|\widehat J\|_2/s$. Final real-component division adds the factor $1+u$ to that error and at most $u\|BR\|_F$. Thus $\|\widehat M-BR\|_F\le\chi\|B\|_F\|R\|_2$. Step 2.1 proves the stated $e_M$ and $\|\widehat M\|_F\le(1+\omega_2)\|B\|_F\|D^{-1}\|_2$. For a scalar pivot the direct real-component divisions instead give these bounds with $\omega_1=u$. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

The update dot bound [F2] gives $\|\widehat Z-\widehat MB^*\|_F\le g_k\|\widehat M\|_F\|B\|_F$. Replacing $\widehat M$ by $M$ adds at most $e_M\|B\|_2$. Final subtraction adds at most $u(\|C\|_F+\|\widehat Z\|_F)$. Combining these with step 3.1 gives raw Schur error at most $u\|C\|_F+q_k\|B\|_F^2\|D^{-1}\|_2$. The exact Schur complement is Hermitian. Copying one chosen computed triangle doubles at most the squared Frobenius error; projecting the diagonal to its real part decreases error. Thus $\|\Delta\|_2\le\beta$. Finally $\|C\|_F\le\sqrt t\|C\|_2$ and $\|B\|_F^2\le k\|B\|_2^2$, proving the stated $\eta_{k,t}$ bound. Empty trailing arrays have zero residual. [F1, F2, F3, step 3.1, algebra]

Put $H=\widehat M-M$. Direct block multiplication gives the displayed full residual, because $N=HD$ and $\widehat MD\widehat M^*-MB^*=HB^*+\widehat MN^*$. The Hermitian off-diagonal matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&N^*\\N&0\end{pmatrix}$ has norm $\|N\|_2$: its square is block diagonal with $N^*N,NN^*$, or equivalently use the defining singular-value maximum. Also $\|N\|_2\le e_M\|D\|_2$. Triangle inequality and step 4.1 therefore give $\|F\|_2\le f$. Every coefficient is an explicit finite function under successful certification, and tends to zero linearly for a fixed nonsingular normalized pivot as $u\to0$. [F3, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

thm-block-ldl-star-residual-with-actual-.actual_claim_text:
Consider a successful run of [[alg-symmetric-indefinite-block-ldl-star]] on a Hermitian input with its declared permutation $P$ and fixed pivot-block sequence. In every formula, $\|X\|_2$ is the operator norm induced by the Euclidean inner products. At stage $r$, write the active matrix as
$$\begin{pmatrix}D_r&B_r^*\\B_r&C_r\end{pmatrix}.$$
Suppose the computed trailing block is
$$\widehat S_{r+1}=C_r-B_rD_r^{-1}B_r^*+\Delta_r,$$
where $\Delta_r$ is the exact local update residual. Embed it into the full permuted coordinates as $E_r$, with zeros on all previously eliminated and current pivot indices. Let $T_r$ be the $n\times n$ identity on previously eliminated coordinates and the padded unit lower block elimination matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\B_rD_r^{-1}&I\end{pmatrix}$$
on the current pivot and trailing coordinates. Set $W_1=I$ and $W_r=T_1\cdots T_{r-1}$ for $r>1$. Then
$$\|PAP^*-L_{\rm ex}D_{\rm blk}L_{\rm ex}^*\|_2 \le\sum_r\|W_r\|_2^2\|\Delta_r\|_2 \le\rho_{\rm blk}\sum_r\eta_r\bigl(\|C_r\|_2+\|B_r\|_2^2\|D_r^{-1}\|_2\bigr),$$
provided the actual local residuals satisfy
$$\|\Delta_r\|_2\le\eta_r\bigl(\|C_r\|_2+\|B_r\|_2^2\|D_r^{-1}\|_2\bigr).$$
Here $L_{\rm ex}$ is the product of the exact-multiplier transformations $T_r$, not a rounded stored multiplier factor. For a nonempty run, $\rho_{\rm blk}:=\max_r\|W_r\|_2^2$ is the actual amplification from this pivot sequence. For an empty pivot partition set $\rho_{\rm blk}=0$; all stage sums are then zero. The trailing-only statement is conditional in this general form. For the specified kernel, [[lem-hermitian-block-ldl-kernel-roundoff-and-reconstruction-residual]] proves it with $\eta_r=\eta_{k_r,t_r}$, retaining the actual normalized-determinant and range certificates. It makes no uniform smallness claim for $\rho_{\rm blk}$, $\|D_r^{-1}\|_2$, or $\eta_r$.

In exact arithmetic every accepted block is nonsingular and each update has $\Delta_r=0$, so a successful run returns $PAP^*=LD_{\rm blk}L^*$.

For the actual rounded output use $\widehat T_r$ built from stored $\widehat M_r$, its full reconstruction residual $F_r$ from the local kernel lemma, and padded products $\widehat W_r=\widehat T_1\cdots\widehat T_{r-1}$. Then
$$PAP^*-\widehat LD_{\rm blk}\widehat L^*=\sum_r\widehat W_rF_r\widehat W_r^*,\qquad \|PAP^*-\widehat LD_{\rm blk}\widehat L^*\|_2\le\sum_r\|\widehat W_r\|_2^2 f_r\le\widehat\rho_{\rm blk}\sum_r f_r,$$
where $f_r$ is the proved explicit local bound. For a nonempty run set $\widehat\rho_{\rm blk}=\max_r\|\widehat W_r\|_2^2$, and for an empty pivot partition set $\widehat\rho_{\rm blk}=0$. This includes multiplier coupling residuals as well as trailing updates. Neither actual growth nor inverse-pivot conditioning is assumed uniformly small.

current_proof_steps.text: For each accepted block, $D_r$ is invertible by its pivot test. Direct block multiplication gives [given, F1, algebra] $$\begin{pmatrix}D_r&B_r^*\\B_r&C_r\end{pmatrix} =\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\B_rD_r^{-1}&I\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}D_r&0\\0&C_r-B_rD_r^{-1}B_r^*\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}I&D_r^{-1}B_r^*\\0&I\end{pmatrix},$$ with the right-hand side an ordinary matrix product. Thus in exact arithmetic each elimination step is a valid Hermitian congruence and, when all stages finish, their product is $PAP^*=LD_{\rm blk}L^*$. [given, F1, algebra]

With a computed update, the middle trailing block differs by $\Delta_r$. Hence the reconstructed active matrix at stage $r$ differs from the block factorization with $\widehat S_{r+1}$ by the embedded matrix whose only nonzero block is $-\Delta_r$ in the trailing coordinates. [given, F1, base, algebra]

Substitute the next-stage factorization into the trailing block of step 1.2. The local residual from stage $r+1$ is conjugated by the padded stage-$r$ lower elimination transformation. Repeated substitution therefore yields [step 1.2, F1, IH, induction, algebra] $$PAP^*-L_{\rm ex}D_{\rm blk}L_{\rm ex}^*=-\sum_r W_r E_r W_r^*.$$ After one stage this is step 1.2. Replacing the next trailing block adds $-T_1E_2T_1^*$; each later substitution adds the next embedded residual conjugated by all preceding $T_h$. Induction on the number of processed pivot blocks gives exactly $W_r=T_1\cdots T_{r-1}$ and the displayed identity. [step 1.2, F1, induction, algebra]

For any compatible maps $X,Y$, [F2] gives $\|XYv\|_2\le\|X\|_2\|Yv\|_2\le\|X\|_2\|Y\|_2\|v\|_2$, so $\|XY\|_2\le\|X\|_2\|Y\|_2$. If $E_r$ is the zero-padded trailing block $\Delta_r$, then $\|E_r x\|_2=\|\Delta_r x_{\rm tail}\|_2\le\|\Delta_r\|_2\|x_{\rm tail}\|_2\le\|\Delta_r\|_2\|x\|_2$, hence $\|E_r\|_2\le\|\Delta_r\|_2$. Also $\|X^*\|_2=\|X\|_2$: express the Euclidean norm as $\sup_{\|v\|=1}|\langle v,w\rangle|$ by Cauchy-Schwarz and take the two finite unit-vector suprema in either order. These inequalities and the triangle inequality bound each summand in step 2.1 by $\|W_r\|_2^2\|\Delta_r\|_2$ and give the first asserted bound. [F2, step 2.1, algebra]

Apply [A1] to each $\Delta_r$ in step 3.1 and use $\|W_r\|_2^2\le\rho_{\rm blk}$. Summing gives the second bound. Since every $D_r$ is invertible but may be ill-conditioned and the transformation products may grow, no universal stability constant follows. [step 3.1, A1, discharge-induction, algebra]

For each accepted concrete kernel apply [F3]. Its $\eta_{k_r,t_r}$ supplies [A1], so steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 3.1, and 4.1 give the claimed trailing-only estimate for the conceptual $L_{\rm ex}$. For actual stored multipliers, [F3] instead gives the active identity $A_r=\widehat T_r\operatorname{diag}(D_r,\widehat S_{r+1})\widehat T_r^*+F_r$, including the off-diagonal residual $N_r=\widehat M_rD_r-B_r$. [F3, step 4.1, algebra]

Substitute the next active identity into the previous trailing block. After one stage the reconstruction residual is $F_1$; each additional stage adds its padded $F_r$ conjugated by all preceding stored-multiplier transformations. Induction gives $PAP^*-\widehat LD_{\rm blk}\widehat L^*=\sum_r\widehat W_rF_r\widehat W_r^*$. The same submultiplicativity from step 3.1 and [F3] give the actual-growth bound. In exact arithmetic every local multiplier and Schur residual is zero, recovering the original exact factorization. [F1, F2, F3, step 3.1, step 5.1, induction, discharge-induction, algebra] ∎

thm-multifrontal-elimination-equivalence.actual_claim_text:
Assume exact arithmetic, a Hermitian positive-definite $A$, and a successful ordered factorization using [[alg-multifrontal-cholesky-and-sparse-triangular-solves]]. The fronts and contribution arrays give the same Cholesky factor as scalar elimination in ordering $\pi$. With $d_r=\ell_r+1=|F_r|$, the arithmetic work for assembly and scalar front updates is
$$O\!\left(\sum_{r=1}^n d_r^2\right),$$
the symbolic factor allocation has exactly $\sum_{r=1}^n d_r$ positions, and each forward/back substitution solve uses $O(\sum_r d_r)$ scalar operations. These are arithmetic and factor-storage counts; they are not wall-clock or total workspace bounds.

current_proof_steps.text:
For each vertex $v_r$, let $T_r$ be its subtree in the elimination forest and let $X_r=F_r\setminus\{v_r\}$. Define the local matrix for $T_r$ on $T_r\cup X_r$ to contain exactly the original entries assigned to fronts in $T_r$; its $X_r	imes X_r$ block is zero, since entries wholly within $X_r$ are assigned to later fronts. If $u\in T_r$ and $w
otin T_r\cup X_r$ had an original edge, then either $w$ is earlier than $u$, making $u$ a later filled neighbor and ancestor of $w$, which would put $w$ in $T_r$, or $w$ is later than $u$, making $w$ a later filled neighbor and ancestor of $u$. In the latter case, repeated application of the child-column containment in [F2] from $u$ up to $v_r$ puts $w$ in $F_r$; since $w
e v_r$ and $w
otin T_r$, it belongs to $X_r$. Both cases contradict the choice of $w$ by [F2,F3]. The induction invariant is that the returned array is the Schur contribution on $X_r$ after eliminating $T_r$ from this local matrix. If $v_r$ is a leaf, every entry assigned to its front has at least one endpoint $v_r$, so its initialized front is exactly this local matrix, with zero external-external block. The scalar update $C-bb^*/d$ therefore returns its Schur contribution. [given, F1, F2, F3, base, induction]

Let $v_r$ have children $v_{s_1},\ldots,v_{s_q}$. By [F2], each child interface $X_{s_h}$ lies in $F_r$, so every extend-add is defined. By [F3], there is no original matrix coupling between interiors of distinct child subtrees: such an edge would make its later endpoint a filled neighbor outside the earlier endpoint's parent path. Form the local matrix on the union of those child interiors and $F_r$, using only original entries assigned to these child subtrees or to $v_r$ and leaving entries wholly in $X_r$ zero. Its child-interior block is $D=\operatorname{diag}(D_1,\ldots,D_q)$, and its coupling to the current front is $B=[B_1\ \cdots\ B_q]$ partitioned by child subtree. Each $D_h=A[T_{s_h},T_{s_h}]$ is a principal submatrix of the positive-definite $A$, so it is positive definite; [F5] gives a Cholesky factor with positive diagonal and therefore shows $D_h$ is nonsingular. Its Schur complement on the current front is $C-BD^{-1}B^*=C-\sum_hB_hD_h^{-1}B_h^*$. The correction $-BD^{-1}B^*=-\sum_hB_hD_h^{-1}B_h^*$ is exactly the sum of child contributions by the induction invariant; adding them to the entries assigned to $v_r$ assembles this same local Schur complement. The pivot update $C-bb^*/d$ then eliminates $v_r$ and proves the invariant for $T_r$. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F3, F5, IH, induction, algebra]

The invariant at each root eliminates all vertices. Each pivot column is therefore computed from the same exact Schur complement as scalar elimination in $\pi$, so the multifrontal factors equal the scalar Cholesky factors. [step 2.1, F1, algebra]

Front $r$ has $d_r=\ell_r+1$ indices. Its dense scalar pivot update and initialization from assigned entries use at most a constant multiple of $d_r^2$ arithmetic operations. Embedding and adding a child contribution touches at most that child's dense trailing block, whose entries are already counted by the child's $d_s^2$ bound. Summing over fronts gives $O(\sum_r d_r^2)$ arithmetic work. By [F1], each factor column retains one diagonal slot and all $\ell_r$ later-neighbor slots, including structural zeros, so symbolic factor storage is exactly $\sum_r d_r$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, F2, algebra]

The forward column updates in [F1] solve $Lx=Pb$: after column $j$ is processed, row $j$ satisfies its equation, and the pivot contribution has been subtracted from each later row. This is the unique solution in [F4]. The descending conjugate updates solve $L^*y=x$ by the backward recurrence in [F4]. Since $PAP^*=LL^*$, these equations imply $PAP^*y=Pb$; multiplying by $P^*$ gives $A(P^*y)=b$. Thus $P^*y$ is the unique solution of $Az=b$. [step 3.1, F1, F4, algebra]

Each stored off-diagonal factor entry is visited once in each triangular solve, with one multiply and one subtraction; each diagonal contributes one division. Hence the two solves use $O(n+\sum_r\ell_r)=O(\sum_r d_r)$ operations, separate from the factorization work in step 3.2. [step 3.2, step 4.1, F1, algebra]

Step 3.1 gives scalar equivalence, step 3.2 gives factorization work and factor storage, and steps 4.1–5.1 give solve correctness and work. [step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, discharge-induction] ∎

thm-nested-dissection-grid-work-and-stor.actual_claim_text:
Let $d\in\{2,3\}$, $k\ge2$, and $n=k^d$. Identify the coordinate grid $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}^d$ with the zero-based matrix indices by the lexicographic bijection in [[alg-nested-dissection-ordering-on-regular-grids]]. Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite, with structural graph a subgraph of the $d$-dimensional nearest-neighbor grid. Under the coordinate nested-dissection ordering, exact scalar multifrontal Cholesky has
$$\begin{array}{c|c|c} d&\text{arithmetic work}&\text{symbolic factor storage}\\ 2&O(n^{3/2})&O(n\log n)\\ 3&O(n^2)&O(n^{4/3}). \end{array}$$
The storage is the number of allocated factor entries, including structural zeros, and excludes temporary contribution arrays. The bounds use the stated grid geometry; they assert no general-graph bound. For $k=1$, there is one pivot and both work and factor storage are $O(1)$.

current_proof_steps.text: If a box side has length $m\ge2$, the median rule leaves each child side with length at most $\lceil m/2\rceil$; a side of length $1$ stays $1$. Iterating gives side lengths at depth $r$ at most $s_r=\lceil k/2^r\rceil$. There are at most $2^{dr}$ boxes at that depth because each box has at most $2^d$ children. By depth $R=\lceil\log_2 k\rceil$, every side has length $1$, so all remaining boxes are terminal. For $0\le r\le R$, $k/2^r\ge1/2$, hence $s_r\le2k/2^r$. [F1, induction, algebra]

If $k=1$, the grid and its ordering contain one terminal pivot and its factor column contains only the diagonal. Hence $d_v=1$ for its unique vertex, and [F3] gives $O(1)$ work and exactly one stored factor entry. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

Let $G'$ be the structural graph of $A$ and let $G$ be the full nearest-neighbor grid on the same vertices. They use the same coordinate ordering. If a pair is an edge in a filled graph of $G'$, [F3] supplies a witness walk in $G'$ with internal vertices eliminated earlier; since $G'$ is a subgraph of $G$, the same walk witnesses that edge in the corresponding filled graph of $G$. Thus every later filled neighbor in $G'$ is also one in $G$, and each subgraph column size is at most the full-grid column size. Fix a box at depth $r$. Its separator has at most $d s_r^{d-1}$ vertices by the union bound over its at most $d$ median hyperplanes; the terminal singleton satisfies the same bound. By [F2], each such pivot has full-grid column size at most $3d s_r^{d-1}$, so the same bound holds for $A$. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

The factorization work contributed by one depth-$r$ box is therefore at most a constant depending only on $d$ times $s_r^{d-1}s_r^{2(d-1)}=s_r^{3(d-1)}$, using [F4]. Summing over at most $2^{dr}$ boxes at each depth and using $s_r\le2k/2^r$ gives [step 1.3, F4, algebra] $$ O\!\left(k^{3(d-1)}\sum_{r=0}^{R}2^{-r(2d-3)}\right). $$ For $d=2$, the geometric ratio is $2^{-1}$, so this is $O(k^3)$. For $d=3$, the ratio is $2^{-3}$, so it is $O(k^6)$. [step 1.3, F3, algebra]

The storage contributed by one depth-$r$ box is at most a constant times $s_r^{d-1}s_r^{d-1}=s_r^{2(d-1)}$, again by [F2] and [F4]. Summing over boxes and using $s_r\le2k/2^r$ gives [step 1.3, F2, F4, algebra] $$ O\!\left(k^{2(d-1)}\sum_{r=0}^{R}2^{-r(d-2)}\right). $$ For $d=2$, there are $O(\log k)$ equal-order terms, giving $O(k^2\log k)$. For $d=3$, the series is bounded by $\sum_{r\ge0}2^{-r}=2$, giving $O(k^4)$. [step 1.3, F2, F3, algebra]

When $d=2$, $n=k^2$ gives $k^3=n^{3/2}$ and $k^2\log k=O(n\log n)$ for $k\ge2$. When $d=3$, $n=k^3$ gives $k^6=n^2$ and $k^4=n^{4/3}$. Thus steps 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 give the displayed rates and the $k=1$ case. The proof used the coordinate-box and grid-boundary counts in [F1]–[F2] together with the fill containment proved in step 1.3, so it does not imply a bound for arbitrary graphs. [step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra] ∎

thm-sparse-cholesky-structural-pattern-w.actual_claim_text:
Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ be Hermitian positive definite and use its pattern from [[def-hermitian-structural-graph-adapter]]. The local Hermitian Schur-support lemma [[lem-hermitian-schur-support-is-contained-in-structural-fill]] applies. In exact arithmetic, the Cholesky recurrence in [[alg-sparse-cholesky-with-invalid-pivot-status]] returns the unique factor $L$ satisfying $PAP^*=LL^*$ and positive diagonal, and every nonzero strict-lower entry of $L$ is permitted by the filled graph $G^+_\pi$.

For $i>j$ with $\{i,j\}\in E^+_\pi$ (where ordered position $i$ represents original vertex $v_i$), define the recurrence numerator
$$\nu_{ij}=B_{ij}-\sum_{k<j}l_{ik}\overline{l_{jk}},\qquad B=PAP^*.$$
If $\nu_{ij}\ne0$ at every permitted strict-lower position, then the numerical nonzero pattern of $L$ is exactly the lower-triangular part of $G^+_\pi$ together with its diagonal. Without this no-cancellation hypothesis only the upper-pattern inclusion is asserted.

current_proof_steps.text: A permutation preserves positive definiteness: for $x\ne0$, $P^*x\ne0$ and $x^*Bx=(P^*x)^*A(P^*x)>0$. Thus [F3] gives a unique exact Cholesky factor $R$ of $B$. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

We show the recurrence in [F1] recovers $R$ column by column, beginning with $j=0$ where the sum is empty. From $B=RR^*$, its $(j,j)$ entry is $B_{jj}=\sum_{k<j}|r_{jk}|^2+|r_{jj}|^2$; since $r_{jj}>0$, the computed exact pivot is $d_j=|r_{jj}|^2>0$ and its positive square root is $r_{jj}$. [step 1.1, F1, F3, base, algebra]

For $i>j$, the $(i,j)$ entry of $B=RR^*$ is $B_{ij}=\sum_{k<j}r_{ik}\overline{r_{jk}}+r_{ij}\overline{r_{jj}}$. Because $r_{jj}>0$, solving this identity for $r_{ij}$ gives exactly the recurrence in [F1]. Induction on $j$ therefore makes every computed column equal to the corresponding column of $R$. [step 2.1, F1, IH, induction, algebra]

Let $S^j$ be the exact Schur complement after eliminating positions $0,\ldots,j-1$ from $B$. Initially $S^0=B$. If the first $j$ columns equal those of $R$, then [step 3.1, F1, F2, IH, induction, algebra]
$$S^j_{ab}=B_{ab}-\sum_{k<j}r_{ak}\overline{r_{bk}}.$$
This identity holds at $j=0$; eliminating pivot $j$ subtracts $r_{aj}\overline{r_{bj}}$ because $S^j_{jj}=r_{jj}^2$ and $S^j_{aj}=r_{aj}r_{jj}$, so it holds at $j+1$. In particular the recurrence numerator at position $(i,j)$ is $S^j_{ij}$. By [F2], a nonzero such entry can occur only on an edge of the filled graph. Therefore every structurally absent position has zero numerator and is correctly omitted, proving the factor support inclusion. [step 3.1, F1, F2, induction, algebra]

Steps 2.1 and 3.1 establish that the exact algorithm returns the unique Cholesky factor; step 4.1 proves the structural upper pattern in the complex Hermitian case; step 5.1 proves equality precisely under the no-cancellation hypothesis. No finite-precision success or stability claim follows from this exact-arithmetic theorem. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, discharge-induction] ∎

thm-threshold-sparse-lu-residual-with-gr.actual_claim_text:
Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be nonsingular, $n\ge1$, and run [[alg-threshold-partial-pivot-sparse-lu]] with $\theta\in(0,1]$. Assume a successful run under the real operation model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]], with unit roundoff $u<1$ and every exact intermediate either zero or normal. Let $M=\max_{i,j}|a_{ij}|>0$, let $S^{(k)}$ be the active matrix at stage $k$ including its current pivot row, and define the actual growth of this run by
$$
\rho=\frac{\max_{k,i,j}|S^{(k)}_{ij}|}{M}\ge1.
$$
For its computed factors and accumulated row permutation, there is a residual $\Delta A$ such that
$$\widehat QPA P^T+\Delta A=\widehat L\widehat U, \qquad \max_{i,j}|\Delta A_{ij}|\le \frac{8nu}{\theta}\rho M, \qquad \|\Delta A\|_\infty\le \frac{8n^2u}{\theta}\rho M, \qquad \|X\|_\infty:=\max_i\sum_j|X_{ij}|.$$
The bound retains this run's actual growth $\rho$ and makes no uniform small-growth claim. This residual theorem is for real arithmetic; the local operation model used here does not specify a general complex division primitive.

current_proof_steps.text: The initial active matrix is $PAP^T$, whose entrywise maximum is $M$ because $P$ only permutes rows and columns; hence $\rho\ge1$. Let $c=S^{(k)}_{ik}$ and $p=S^{(k)}_{kk}$ at a successful pivot. If the diagonal is accepted, [F1] gives $|c/p|\le\theta^{-1}$. If a maximum-modulus entry is selected, $|c/p|\le1\le\theta^{-1}$. The rounded division therefore gives $|\widehat l_{ik}|\le(1+u)/\theta\le2/\theta$. Also every pivot-row entry and every active entry has modulus at most $\rho M$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

For a trailing update, write $p_{ij}=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj})$ and $S^{(k+1)}_{ij}=\operatorname{fl}(S^{(k)}_{ij}-p_{ij})$. Define $e_{ijk}=S^{(k+1)}_{ij}-(S^{(k)}_{ij}-\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj})$. By [F2]. [given, F1, F2, algebra]
$$|p_{ij}-\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj}|\le u|\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj}|, \quad |S^{(k+1)}_{ij}-(S^{(k)}_{ij}-p_{ij})|\le u|S^{(k)}_{ij}-p_{ij}|.$$
The triangle inequality and $|p_{ij}|\le(1+u)|\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj}|$ yield
$$|e_{ijk}|\le u|S^{(k)}_{ij}|+u(2+u)|\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj}| \le u\rho M\left(1+\frac{(2+u)(1+u)}{\theta}\right) \le \frac{7u\rho M}{\theta},$$
using $u<1$ and $\theta\le1$. [step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

For a computed multiplier, $\widehat l_{ik}=\operatorname{fl}(c/p)$, so [F2] gives a division residual $e^{\rm div}_{ik}:=c-\widehat l_{ik}p$ with $|e^{\rm div}_{ik}|\le u|c|\le u\rho M$. [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

Track each active row together with its previously stored entries of $\widehat L$ and its accumulated update residuals. Before stage $k$, for every active row $i$ and active column $j\ge k$, maintain [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1, induction, algebra]
$$
(Q_k P A P^T)_{ij}=\sum_{r<k}\widehat l_{ir}\widehat u_{rj}+S^{(k)}_{ij}-\sum_{r<k}e_{ijr},
$$
where $Q_k$ is the row permutation accumulated so far. At $k=0$ this is $S^{(0)}=PAP^T$. Swapping two active rows also swaps their earlier $L$ entries and residual histories, so it preserves the invariant. After the pivot, $\widehat u_{kj}=S^{(k)}_{kj}$; each lower-row update is $S^{(k+1)}_{ij}=S^{(k)}_{ij}-\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kj}+e_{ijk}$, so substitution gives the same invariant at stage $k+1$. For the pivot column, $S^{(k)}_{ik}=\widehat l_{ik}\widehat u_{kk}+e^{\rm div}_{ik}$ by definition of the division residual. Thus after all stages, for $i\le j$,
$$
(\widehat QPA P^T)_{ij}-(\widehat L\widehat U)_{ij}=-\sum_{k<i}e_{ijk},
$$
and for $i>j$,
$$(\widehat QPA P^T)_{ij}-(\widehat L\widehat U)_{ij} =e^{\rm div}_{ij}-\sum_{k<j}e_{ijk}.$$
These identities define $\Delta A=\widehat L\widehat U-\widehat QPA P^T$. Each entry contains at most $n$ update residuals and at most one division residual. [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1, induction, algebra]

By steps 1.2–2.1, every residual entry is bounded by [step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]
$$n\frac{7u\rho M}{\theta}+u\rho M \le \frac{8nu}{\theta}\rho M,$$
since $n\ge1$ and $\theta\le1$. Summing at most $n$ such bounds in any row gives $\|\Delta A\|_\infty\le8n^2u\rho M/\theta$. [step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

The definition of $\Delta A$ in step 3.1 gives the displayed nearby-factorization identity, and step 4.1 gives both residual bounds. The only growth quantity in the estimate is the maximum active-entry magnitude of this executed run. [step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

alg-householder-bidiagonalization.actual_claim_text:
Let $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, where $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$. Put $p=\min(m,n)$ and $M=\max(m,n)$. If $m\ge n$, set $C=A$; if $m<n$, set $C=A^*$. Thus $C\in\mathbb F^{M\times p}$.

Save the input as $C_0=C$ and initialize $U=I_M$, $V=I_p$, and empty ordered lists of stored local left and right transformations. For $k=1,\ldots,p$, in this order:

1. Let $x=C_{k:M,k}$. If $x=0$, use the identity left transformation. Otherwise choose $\phi=x_1/|x_1|$ when $x_1\ne0$ and $\phi=1$ when $x_1=0$, set $\alpha=-\phi\|x\|_2$, $v=x-\alpha e_1$, and $h=v/\|v\|_2$. Use the Householder reflector $H=I-2hh^*$ on rows $k:M$. Update $C\leftarrow H^*C$ on those rows and append this local transformation to the left list. In exact arithmetic update $U\leftarrow U\operatorname{diag}(I_{k-1},H)$. In finite precision update columns $k:M$ of the dense accumulator $U$ by right application of the same stored local reflector data, using the separate-block branch of [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]] and making no target-zero write to $U$.
2. If $k<p$, let $y=C_{k,k+1:p}^*$. If $y=0$, use the identity right transformation. Otherwise apply the same phase and normalization rule to $y$ to form the Householder reflector $G$, then apply $C\leftarrow C\operatorname{diag}(I_k,G)$ and append this local transformation to the right list. In exact arithmetic update $V\leftarrow V\operatorname{diag}(I_k,G)$. In finite precision update columns $k+1:p$ of the dense accumulator $V$ by right application of the same stored local reflector data, using the separate-block branch of [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]] and making no target-zero write to $V$.

The exact arithmetic output is the leading $p\times p$ upper bidiagonal block $B$ of $C$, together with $U,V$. For $m\ge n$ the output relation is $U^*AV=\begin{bmatrix}B\\0\end{bmatrix}$. For $m<n$ it is $U^*A^*V=\begin{bmatrix}B\\0\end{bmatrix}$; equivalently $A=V\begin{bmatrix}B^*&0\end{bmatrix}U^*$.

In finite precision, each left/right reflector uses [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]], including its real/complex scaled formation, range checks and exact target-column/row zero writes. This is the arithmetic realization of the exact steps above. A zero active vector takes the identity branch. Any nonfinite intermediate or overflow returns `range-failure` with the partial factors and stored local transformations; otherwise return `success`, $B,U,V$, the ordered stored local transformations, the reconstruction residual $\|C_0-U\begin{bmatrix}B\\0\end{bmatrix}V^*\|_F$, and the two orthogonality residuals $\|U^*U-I\|_F$ and $\|V^*V-I\|_F$. The reconstruction uses the saved input $C_0$, not the overwritten work matrix. The exact products of the stored unitary representatives are the theoretical factors; the dense finite-precision accumulators are rounded and their residuals are computed quantities, not certified bounds by themselves. Matrix residuals use the Frobenius norm defined in [[def-frobenius-matrix-norm]].

alg-implicit-shifted-bidiagonal-qr-with-.actual_claim_text:
Input the original $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, the successful output record of [[alg-householder-bidiagonalization]] for $C=A$ if $m\ge n$ and $C=A^*$ otherwise, a deflation tolerance $\tau\ge0$, and a finite nonnegative integer sweep budget $N$. The reduction record supplies the upper bidiagonal work matrix $B_0$, dense accumulators $U_B,V_B$, and ordered stored local transformation data. Initialize $B=B_0$, the sweep accumulators $U_\Sigma,V_\Sigma$ to identities of order $p=\min(m,n)$, empty ordered left/right transformation lists, an empty deflation record, a pass counter $t=0$, and a sweep counter $s=0$. Write the diagonal as $d_i$ and superdiagonal as $e_i$, and set $e_0=0$.

At the start of each pass, set $t\leftarrow t+1$, set $e_i$ to zero and append $(t,i,e_i^{old})$ to the deflation record whenever $|e_i|\le\tau(|d_i|+|d_{i+1}|)$. The corresponding additive matrix change has entry $-e_i^{old}$ at $(i,i+1)$ and zero elsewhere. Record any later non-target sparsity cleanup the same way with its row, column, and old value. The zero entries split the active blocks. If every active block has size one, stop with `converged`. Otherwise process the active blocks in increasing order of $\ell$, skipping singleton blocks. Before each block sweep, if $s=N$, stop with `budget-exhausted`; otherwise form only the tridiagonal entries of $T=B^*B$ on that block: $T_{ii}=|d_i|^2+|e_{i-1}|^2$ and $T_{i,i+1}=\overline{d_i}e_i$. Choose $\mu$ to be the eigenvalue of the trailing Hermitian block $\begin{bmatrix}T_{r-1,r-1}&T_{r-1,r}\\T_{r,r-1}&T_{rr}\end{bmatrix}$ closest to $T_{rr}$, resolving a tie by the smaller eigenvalue. If the leading pivot $d_\ell$ is zero or has magnitude at most $\tau\max(|e_{\ell-1}|,|e_\ell|)$, use the zero-shift branch $\mu=0$ and choose the initial right Givens factor $G_\ell$ so that $(d_\ell,e_\ell)G_\ell=(\rho,0)$, avoiding division by the small or zero diagonal.

In the ordinary branch choose the first right Givens factor $G_\ell$ so that $G_\ell^*(T_{\ell\ell}-\mu,T_{\ell+1,\ell})^T=(\rho,0)^T$, where $T_{\ell+1,\ell}=\overline{e_\ell}d_\ell$. In either branch, apply $B\leftarrow BG_\ell$, update columns $\ell,\ell+1$ of $V_\Sigma$ by right multiplication by this same stored rotation, and append its exact unitary representative to the right list. For $j=\ell,\ldots,r-1$, choose a left Givens factor $H_j$ so that $H_j^*(B_{j,j},B_{j+1,j})^T=(\rho,0)^T$; apply it to rows $j,j+1$, update columns $j,j+1$ of $U_\Sigma$ by right multiplication by this same stored rotation, and append its exact unitary representative to the left list. If $j<r-1$, choose a right Givens factor $G_{j+1}$ so that $(B_{j,j+1},B_{j,j+2})G_{j+1}=(\rho,0)$; apply it to columns $j+1,j+2$, update the corresponding columns of $V_\Sigma$ by right multiplication by this same stored rotation, and append its exact unitary representative to the right list. Continue until the bulge reaches the active block endpoint. A zero annihilation vector uses the identity rotation. In finite precision each Givens formation/update uses [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]], conjugate-transposed as needed for the stated left/right orientation; accumulator multiplications use the same stored local data but omit all target-zero writes. The dense accumulator multiplications follow the operationwise arithmetic model, while the ordered lists retain the exact unitary representatives used in analysis. Target zero writes to $B$ are included in their local error bounds. The initial shift-vector rotation does not zero an unrelated entry of $B$. Each Givens factor is chosen using [[def-real-and-complex-givens-transformations]] and its annihilation guarantee in [[thm-householder-reflectors-and-givens-transformations-are-unitary-and-annihilate-targeted-entries]].

After each processed block, increment $s$ by one. Once all current active blocks have been processed, start a new pass. If any operation, norm or pivot is invalid or nonfinite, or a nonzero exact intermediate is outside the normal range, return `range-failure` with the partial $B$, accumulators, transformation lists, deflation record, and available residual reports. On `budget-exhausted`, return the current $B$, diagonal candidates, accumulators, transformation lists, deflation record, triplet residuals, and orthogonality residuals. On `converged`, return $B_{final}$ (diagonal), the candidate singular values obtained by the scaled two-component modulus evaluation of its diagonal entries (real absolute value is exact), both dense accumulators, both transformation lists, the deflation record, and triplet/orthogonality residuals; also return its tall embedding $\overline B_{final}=\begin{bmatrix}B_{final}\\0_{M-p,p}\end{bmatrix}$. For a nonconverged block, candidates are estimates only and carry no accuracy claim.

Let $W_B=\operatorname{diag}(U_\Sigma,I_{M-p})$. In exact arithmetic the tall-orientation accumulated factors are $U_C=U_BW_B$ and $V_C=V_BV_\Sigma$. In finite precision form each dense product by row-by-column multiplication, with six-real-operation complex products and sequential componentwise rounded additions under the operationwise model; return `range-failure` if any required intermediate is invalid, nonfinite, or outside the normal range. Their exact theoretical factors are the products represented by the ordered local transformation lists together with the bidiagonal-reduction lists. If $m\ge n$, set $\widehat U=U_C$ and $\widehat V=V_C$; for each nonzero diagonal entry $d_i$ of $B_{final}$, multiply column $i$ of $\widehat U$ by $d_i/|d_i|$ in exact arithmetic, using componentwise division by the successful scaled modulus readout in finite precision. If $m<n$, set $\widehat U=V_C$ and $\widehat V=U_C$; in this wide orientation multiply column $i$ of $\widehat V$ by $d_i/|d_i|$ instead. This phase placement makes the exact singular-value factorization nonnegative in both orientations and keeps the left/right vector dimensions correct. Sort the candidate values in nonincreasing order, breaking ties by their original diagonal index, and permute the corresponding columns of the returned triplet vectors in the same way; leave $B_{final}$ and the transformation lists in their algorithmic order. For every candidate triplet $(\widehat\sigma_i,\widehat u_i,\widehat v_i)$, report $\|A\widehat v_i-\widehat\sigma_i\widehat u_i\|_2$ and $\|A^*\widehat u_i-\widehat\sigma_i\widehat v_i\|_2$. Also report $\|\widehat U^*\widehat U-I\|_F$ and $\|\widehat V^*\widehat V-I\|_F$. The reports expose finite-budget and rounding behavior; they do not certify convergence by themselves. Matrix residuals use the Frobenius norm defined in [[def-frobenius-matrix-norm]]. Any additional sparsity cleanup is recorded separately in the deflation record with its discarded-entry perturbation.

alg-rank-thresholded-least-squares-by-sv.actual_claim_text:
Input $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, $b\in\mathbb F^m$, a threshold $\tau\ge0$, and a finite nonnegative integer bidiagonal-QR sweep budget $N$, with $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$; vector residuals use the Euclidean norm of [[def-inner-product-norm]]. Compute the Householder bidiagonal reduction and call the finite-budget bidiagonal QR procedure. If either procedure returns a failure or budget-exhausted status, return `inconclusive` with its triplet and orthogonality reports and do not claim a least-squares solution.

For a successful exact SVD record $A=U\Sigma V^*$, set $q=\#\{i:\sigma_i>\tau\}$, form $A_\tau=U\Sigma_\tau V^*$ and the canonical truncated pseudoinverse $A_\tau^+$ of [[def-truncated-singular-value-pseudoinverse-at-a-declared-threshold]], and compute $x_\tau=A_\tau^+b$. Return $x_\tau$, the declared threshold, $q$, the model residual $\|A_\tau x_\tau-b\|_2$, the original residual $\|Ax_\tau-b\|_2$, and the discarded tail size $\sigma_{q+1}$ (defined as $0$ for $q=p=\min(m,n)$). The strict comparison $\sigma_i>\tau$ is used, so values equal to the threshold are discarded. For finite-precision singular-value estimates $(\widehat U,\widehat\Sigma,\widehat V)$, form $\widehat I=\{i:\widehat\sigma_i>\tau\}$, $\widehat A_\tau=\widehat U\widehat\Sigma_\tau\widehat V^*$, and the coordinate candidate $\widehat x=\widehat V\widehat\Sigma_{\widehat I}^{+}\widehat U^*b$, where $\widehat\Sigma_{\widehat I}^{+}$ has diagonal entries $1/\widehat\sigma_i$ for $i\in\widehat I$ and zero otherwise; compute both residuals and label the threshold count `unverified` unless a certified error interval separates every compared value from $\tau$. This finite-precision candidate is not called a certified numerical rank or a minimum-norm least-squares solution.

alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-given.actual_claim_text:
Use the operationwise real/complex arithmetic model, with six-real-operation complex products and componentwise division by positive real scalars. A scaled norm of a nonzero complex vector first chooses the largest absolute real or imaginary component $s>0$, rounds every real component divided by $s$, sums their rounded squares sequentially, rounds the positive square root, and rounds multiplication by $s$. A norm of already scaled components omits the last multiplication. Zero input has exact norm zero. Reject every nonzero exact intermediate outside the normal range, nonfinite/invalid operation, and nonpositive required norm; return the first range-failure. All sign changes and conjugations are exact.

For a Householder active block $C=[x\;B]$, $x\in\mathbb C^r$, a zero $x$ copies the block with identity action. Otherwise compute $\widehat N$ by the scaled norm. If $x_1=0$ put $\widehat\phi=1$; otherwise compute its modulus $\widehat a$ by its own two-component scaled norm and divide its real and imaginary parts by $\widehat a$. Set $\widehat\alpha=-\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\phi\widehat N)$ using real-scalar component multiplication, and $v=\operatorname{fl}(x-\widehat\alpha e_1)$. Compute $w$ by sequential summation of all $2r$ rounded real component squares of $v$, and $\widehat\tau=\operatorname{fl}(2/w)$. Compute $d=\operatorname{fl}(v^*B)$, $p=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\tau v)$, $Z=\operatorname{fl}(pd)$, and $\widehat B=\operatorname{fl}(B-Z)$. Return $C_+=[\widehat\alpha e_1\;\widehat B]$, writing exact zeros below the target diagonal, and store $v,\widehat\tau$. Its theoretical representative is $H(v)=I-2vv^*/(v^*v)$. For a separate block application omit the column overwrite. For a right step apply these instructions to the conjugate-transposed block and transpose back.

For a Givens target pair $(a,b)$, use the identity when $b=0$, including $(0,0)$. Otherwise choose $\lambda$ as the largest absolute real/imaginary component of $(a,b)$, round $z=a/\lambda$ and $w=b/\lambda$ componentwise, and compute $h$ as the norm of their four already scaled components. If $z\ne0$, compute $n_z$ as the norm of its two components, $\widehat\phi=\operatorname{fl}(z/n_z)$, $c=\operatorname{fl}(n_z/h)$ and $s=\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\phi\overline w)/h)$. If $z=0$, set $c=0$ and $s=\operatorname{fl}(\overline w/h)$. Store $T=\begin{pmatrix}c&s\\-\overline s&c\end{pmatrix}$ and apply it to the chosen two rows using two complex products and one rounded componentwise addition for each output entry. For an actual target column, set its intended annihilated entry to exact zero after the update. The initial shift-vector rotation is formed from the shift vector but applied to the matrix without zeroing an unrelated matrix entry. Right applications use the conjugate-transposed form. Its exact unitary representative is $Q=T/\sqrt{c^2+|s|^2}$; this normalization defines a mathematical representative and is not an additional rounded operation.

These are arithmetic realizations of the canonical Householder and Givens methods. Returned dense transformation accumulators may be rounded; the exact unitary products used in backward-error statements are represented by the stored local data. Additional discarded matrix entries must be recorded separately, including their magnitudes. Their omission is never implicit in a sparsity convention.

alg-strong-rank-revealing-qr-with-finite.actual_claim_text:
Input a real or complex matrix $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$ with $m\ge n$, a target $k$ with $0\le k<n$, a factor $f\ge1$, and a finite swap cap $S\in\mathbb N\cup\{0\}$. The exact-arithmetic version is specified below. A finite-precision implementation uses the same branches, tests finiteness after each operation, and returns `range-failure` if a required quantity is nonfinite.

1. If $A$ is not full column rank, return `rank-deficient-input`. Otherwise initialize a column permutation $\Pi$ and the full column-pivoted QR factorization $A\Pi=QR$, where $Q\in\mathbb F^{m\times m}$ is unitary and $R\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$ is upper trapezoidal, using the greedy residual-norm pivot convention. Partition $R=\begin{bmatrix}R_{11}&R_{12}\\0&R_{22}\end{bmatrix}$ after the first $k$ rows and columns. Do not return the reduced QR form. The selected first $k$ columns then have a nonsingular leading block. For $k=0$, return this full factorization with `success`.
2. For $k>0$, refactor the current fixed column order in the full QR form, without further pivoting whenever needed, using unitary Householder or Givens transformations. If the selected leading block is singular, return `singular-selected-block`.
3. Form $X=R_{11}^{-1}R_{12}$. For $1\le i\le k$ let $\omega_i=\|e_i^*R_{11}^{-1}\|_2$; for $1\le j\le n-k$ let $\gamma_j=\|R_{22}(:,j)\|_2$. Define the swap score $s_{ij}=\bigl(|X_{ij}|^2+(\omega_i\gamma_j)^2\bigr)^{1/2}$.
4. If $\max_{i,j}|X_{ij}|>f$, choose the lexicographically first pair attaining the largest $|X_{ij}|$. Otherwise, if $\max_{i,j}s_{ij}>f$, choose the lexicographically first pair attaining the largest score. If neither inequality holds, return `success` and the factors, permutation, $X$, and maximum score. The first branch retains the usual coefficient-triggered swap; the second controls the trailing residual needed for the strong spectral comparison.
5. When a violating pair was chosen, if the swap count is already $S$, return `swap-budget-exhausted` with the current partial factors. Otherwise interchange the chosen selected and trailing columns, restore triangular form with Givens rotations, increment the swap count, and return to step 2. Thus a cap $S\ge\binom nk-1$ is sufficient in exact arithmetic whenever the input is full column rank.

The statuses are `success`, `rank-deficient-input`, `singular-selected-block`, `swap-budget-exhausted`, and `range-failure`. In particular, ordinary column-pivoted QR is only the initialization: the procedure does not assert that its output alone satisfies the strong bounds. Both exact and finite-precision outputs use the full factor shape; exact-arithmetic success satisfies the singular-value comparison theorem. A finite-precision `success` is a candidate until the following certificate is verified. Retain the ordered local transformation data representing an exact unitary product $W$ separately from the rounded dense $Q$. Let $\widehat R$ denote the returned upper trapezoidal matrix. A certificate consists of a nonsingular $\widehat R_{11}$, rigorous upper bounds $b_{ij}$ on the exact real numbers $\bigl(|(\widehat R_{11}^{-1}\widehat R_{12})_{ij}|^2+\|e_i^*\widehat R_{11}^{-1}\|_2^2\|\widehat R_{22}(:,j)\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}$, and $\varepsilon\ge0$ with $\|A\Pi-W\widehat R\|_2\le\varepsilon$. All $b_{ij}\le f$ are required. For $k=0$ there are no score or inverse conditions. The bounds must account for arithmetic and input representation; ordinary rounded score and residual evaluations do not constitute this certificate. Exact arithmetic on represented data or validated outward enclosures may establish it. If certification is unavailable or a bound exceeds its threshold, report `uncertified` for the certificate, retaining the algorithm status and all candidate outputs. A verified certificate gives the residual-adjusted comparisons for the returned blocks even if swaps were stopped by the budget.

cex-classical-column-pivoted-qr-is-not-s.actual_claim_text: Every exact classical column-pivoted QR output satisfies the strong rank-revealing coefficient bound $\max_{i,j}|(R_{11}^{-1}R_{12})_{ij}|\le1$ for every target rank $k$.

current_proof_steps.text: Column $j$ of $A$ has entries $-cs^{i-1}$ for $i<j$, $s^{j-1}$ for $i=j$, and zero below. Its squared norm is $c^2\sum_{r=0}^{j-2}s^{2r}+s^{2(j-1)}=1$, using $c^2=1-s^2$. After the first $r$ columns have been selected, they span the first $r$ coordinate vectors because their leading triangular block has nonzero diagonal. The residual of each remaining column $j>r$ has squared norm $s^{2r}\left(c^2\sum_{t=0}^{j-r-2}s^{2t}+s^{2(j-r-1)}\right)=s^{2r}$ (the sum is empty when $j=r+1$). Thus all remaining residuals tie at every step, and the declared tie rule makes CPQR select columns in their original order. [F3, A1, algebra]

By [F1] and step 1.1, the resulting permutation is the identity. The matrix $A$ is upper triangular with positive diagonal, so the QR factors can be taken as $Q=I$ and $R=A$. For $k=3$, solving $R_{11}x=R_{12}$ gives $x_3=-c$, $x_2=-c(1+c)$, and $x_1=-c(1+c)^2=-9/8$. Hence $\max_i|x_i|\ge9/8>1$, violating the coefficient condition in [F2]. [step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

This CPQR output therefore fails the strong coefficient test with $f=1$. It does not contradict the strong RRQR procedure: that procedure performs additional swaps when its coefficient or combined residual score exceeds the threshold. [step 2.1, F2] ∎

cor-computed-singular-values-absolute-er.actual_claim_text:
Let $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$ and put $C=A$ when $m\ge n$, $C=A^*$ when $m<n$. Suppose a successful computed SVD path in this tall orientation supplies $C+E=\widehat U\begin{bmatrix}\widehat B\\0\end{bmatrix}\widehat V^*$, where $\widehat U\in\mathbb F^{M\times M}$ and $\widehat V\in\mathbb F^{p\times p}$ are the exact unitary products represented by the stored local transformations, $M=\max(m,n)$, $p=\min(m,n)$, and the returned square $\widehat B\in\mathbb F^{p\times p}$ is the diagonal final bidiagonal matrix from [[alg-implicit-shifted-bidiagonal-qr-with-deflation]]. These are the theoretical factors in [[thm-bidiagonal-svd-backward-error-under-local-stability]], separate from the rounded dense accumulators returned for candidate triplets. If the returned values are the exact singular values of $\widehat B$, then for every $1\le i\le p$,
$$|\widehat\sigma_i-\sigma_i(A)|\le\|E\|_2\le\|E\|_F.$$
For actual rounded modulus readout from a diagonal $\widehat B$, let $\epsilon_{\rm read}=((1+u)^4-1)\max_i|d_i|$ for the successful scaled complex modulus algorithm; use zero for exact real absolute values. After ordering the candidates, the bound is $|\widehat\sigma_i-\sigma_i(A)|\le\|E\|_2+\epsilon_{\rm read}$. This assertion applies to a successful, fully reduced result; a finite-budget `budget-exhausted` output has residual reports but no such accuracy conclusion.

current_proof_steps.text: By [F1], $C+E=\widehat U\begin{bmatrix}\widehat B\\0\end{bmatrix}\widehat V^*$. The tall matrix $\begin{bmatrix}\widehat B\\0\end{bmatrix}$ has the singular values of $\widehat B$, since its adjoint times itself is $\widehat B^*\widehat B$; unitary invariance in [F3] therefore gives the ordered singular values $s_i$ for $C+E$. By [F4], $C$ and $A$ have the same $p$ singular values. [F1, F3, F4, algebra]

Apply [F2] to $C$ and $C+E$. It gives $|\sigma_i(C+E)-\sigma_i(C)|\le\|E\|_2$; step 1.1 identifies these singular values with $s_i$ and $\sigma_i(A)$, respectively, and [F3] gives $\|E\|_2\le\|E\|_F$. [step 1.1, F2, F3, algebra]

A scaled modulus of two real components has relative norm factors between $(1-u)^4$ and $(1+u)^4$, by expanding the two scaling operations, square products and sum, square root and rescaling. Hence each rounded magnitude differs from $|d_i|$ by at most $\epsilon_{\rm read}$. If two finite lists differ coordinatewise by at most $\epsilon$, their ordered lists do too: otherwise at the violating rank the count of entries above or below the corresponding threshold contradicts the coordinatewise bounds. Apply this to the diagonal magnitudes and combine with step 2.1. For exact readout $\widehat\sigma_i=s_i$ the first bound follows already from step 2.1; for rounded readout the additional modulus allowance gives the stated extension. Real sign removal is exact. [F5, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
